name: RouterEval II
description: The original RouterEval article proposed a harness for evaluating routing policies rather than individual models: shared datasets, comparable constraints, trace-first evaluation, offline A/B comparisons, shadow evaluation, and behavioral checks. Its sample code illustrated that approach; it did not implement every proposed constraint or safeguard. Those foundations remain useful. But routing policies operate in environments where workloads, models, tools, prices, requirements, and risk profiles change. RouterEval II adds a temporal evaluation layer: versioned production-derived samples, explicit comparison populations, and diagnostics that help distinguish changing traffic from changing system performance. The objective is not unchanging behavior. It is maintaining acceptable quality, cost, latency, and policy compliance as operating conditions change. Distribution changes are reasons to investigate; they do not, by themselves, demonstrate performance deterioration.
